extractions.source_title: Agentic Compilation: Mitigating the LLM Rerun Crisis for Minimized-Inference-Cost Web Automation
extractions.fact: One-shot LLM compilation from natural language intent + DOM Sanitization Module output → deterministic JSON workflow blueprint with semantic selectors
extractions.verbatim_quote: A one-shot LLM invocation processes a token-efficient semantic representation from a DOM Sanitization Module (DSM) and emits a deterministic JSON workflow blueprint. A lightweight runtime then drives the browser without further model queries.
extractions.source_location: Abstract; Section 3.2; Section 4.2 Table 1; Section 4.3 Table 2
extractions.extracted_value: Compilation success rate: 80-94% zero-shot (T1: 92%, T2: 80%, T3: 94%); HITL → near-100%
extractions.runnability_evidence: Requires LLM for compilation phase; execution runtime local (Playwright/Selenium). Not runnable without LLM key.
extractions.task_distribution_comparability: INCOMPARABLE: Live web automation (extraction/form-filling/fingerprinting on real sites) vs SPIDER's locally-served multi-endpoint HTTP with parameterized identifiers (30 orthogonal header/body/auth + 10 mixed routing). Different: browser-required vs no-browser; DOM-based vs API-based; general web vs synthetic routing.
extractions.compilation_vs_inheritance_conflation: CLEAN - Pure compilation-bypass: one-shot LLM → JSON blueprint → zero-LLM execution. Lazy replanning is exception handling, not inheritance.
extractions.staleness_maintenance_reported: Structural UI mutations bi-annually/annually (Section 5.2). Lazy replanning handles selector healing. No explicit maintenance cost reported.

extractions.source_title: Agentic Compilation: Mitigating the LLM Rerun Crisis for Minimized-Inference-Cost Web Automation
extractions.fact: O(M×N) → amortized O(1) inference scaling; per-compilation cost $0.002-$0.092; evaluated at M=500, N=5
extractions.verbatim_quote: We formalize this cost reduction from O(M×N) to amortized O(1) inference scaling, where M is the number of reruns and N is the sequential actions... Total inference cost ranges from $0.002 to $0.10 depending on model selection.
extractions.source_location: Abstract; Section 4.1 Equations 2-3; Section 4.2 Table 1; Section 4.3
extractions.extracted_value: Reuse count: M=500; Build cost: $0.002-$0.092; Task length: N=5; Amortization: O(M×N)→O(1); Staleness: bi-annual UI changes
extractions.task_distribution_comparability: INCOMPARABLE: Live web vs local HTTP; browser vs no browser
extractions.staleness_maintenance_reported: Bi-annual UI changes; lazy replanning for selector healing

extractions.fact: Behavioral recording → determinism census → synthesis/distillation → verification gate → WebAssembly cognition binaries with manifests
extractions.verbatim_quote: Auto... records live agent behavior, measures which parts are secretly deterministic, extracts them into verified programs or distilled specialists, and emits cognition binaries: WebAssembly artifacts whose manifests carry measured guarantees
extractions.source_location: Abstract; Section 1; Section 3 (Recording and the census; IR and passes; Runtime); Section 4 (Verification as the Type System); Section 5.1 Table 1; Section 5.2 Table 2; Section 5.3 Figure 3, Table 3
extractions.extracted_value: Witnessed-deterministic: 87.1% of 560 spans; F1/F3/F4=100%; F2=77.5%; F5=17.5%; F3 refused; F5 FAIL 42.5%; Gate-refused recompilation under unfaithful reference
extractions.runnability_evidence: Runtime: compiled wasm (no LLM). Recording: requires frontier LLM + SDK shims. Requires Rust toolchain + wasmtime.
extractions.task_distribution_comparability: INCOMPARABLE: Auto-Bench (agent spans: ticket triage, inbox pipeline, field extraction, routing, summarization) vs SPIDER alias-OOD (parameterized HTTP routing). Different: agent behavior compilation vs web navigation; recorded spans vs synthetic tasks.
extractions.compilation_vs_inheritance_conflation: CONFLATION FLAGGED - Records live agent behavior (inheritance/behavioral recording) then compiles. Ratchet continuously recompiles from new deopt traces.
extractions.staleness_maintenance_reported: Loose guard (α=0.1) → 48.9% silent wrongness (133/272). Unfaithful deopt reference stalls ratchet. Agent-faithful config closes loop. Semantic embedding guards are recorded upgrade (Section 5.4).

extractions.fact: Ratchet recompiles after K=8 new inputs; 6.4x cost reduction (59→2 μ$/item); steady state 2.3 μ$/item; 3 distribution shifts in 300 items
extractions.verbatim_quote: On a 300-item stream with three scheduled distribution shifts, the closed loop compiles three artifact generations and drives marginal cost from 59 to 2 micro-dollars per item (6.4× end-to-end) at 96.9% parity on witnessed inputs with zero errors.
extractions.source_location: Abstract; Section 5.3 Figure 3; Section 5.3 Table 3; Algorithm 1
extractions.extracted_value: Reuse count: K=8 recompile stride; Witnessed-determinism: 87.1%; Novelty rate: 3 shifts/300 items (56 distinct texts); Build cost: $0.0621 compiler spend; Amortization: 6.4x, steady state 2.3 μ$/item; Staleness: 48.9% silent wrongness under loose guard
extractions.staleness_maintenance_reported: 48.9% silent wrongness; calibration exposure; semantic embedding guards needed

extractions.source_title: TraceCompiler: Skill-Guided Mining and Compilation of LLM Agent Traces into Mostly Deterministic Workflows
extractions.fact: Trace clustering → dependency verification (0.928 precision, 0.943 recall) → provenance classification → executable workflows; refuses under-determined irreversible effects
extractions.verbatim_quote: Mechanized form of the rule recovers producer–consumer dependencies at 0.928 precision and 0.943 recall over 15,775 def–use edges... compiler skill run blind reaches 0.992 on 250 of those edges... Spotify/Todoist intent the compiler correctly refuses to compile, because an irreversible side effect is under-determined.
extractions.source_location: Abstract; Section 3.3; Section 6.1 (Intent 1 Venmo, Intent 2 Spotify/Todoist); Section 6.2; Section 6.3
extractions.extracted_value: Dependency precision/recall: 0.928/0.943; Blind skill: 0.992; AppWorld: 0.993 precision; Venmo: 34→11 calls, 15/21 leave-one-out; Spotify/Todoist: REFUSES to compile
extractions.runnability_evidence: Requires frontier LLM for blind protocol/compilation skill. Mechanized rule model-free. Execution requires AppWorld simulator.
extractions.task_distribution_comparability: INCOMPARABLE: AppWorld (9 apps, 457 APIs, 56 scenarios) + T1 (template travel) vs SPIDER alias-OOD. Different: API call traces vs HTTP routing; requires AppWorld simulator; multi-app coordination vs single-app routing.
extractions.compilation_vs_inheritance_conflation: CONFLATION FLAGGED - Mines from agent traces (behavioral recording): 'Tool-using language-model agents repeatedly rediscover procedures they have already executed, producing traces that mix reusable structure with retries, exploration, accidental ordering, and repeated lookups' (Abstract). Compilation INPUT is inherited/recorded behavior.
extractions.staleness_maintenance_reported: NOT REPORTED. 'We measure call reduction but not offline compilation cost, so we claim no net efficiency result' (Abstract). No compile/decline rate reported over 56 scenarios.

extractions.verbatim_quote: Venmo money-request intent reduces 34 observed API calls to 11 runtime calls... Per scenario the median removable fraction is 51.4% (IQR 41.9–74.1%)... We measure call reduction but not offline compilation cost, so we claim no net efficiency result.
extractions.extracted_value: Reuse count: support floor 5; Call reduction: 34→11, 106→59; Removable fraction: 51.4% median; Build cost: NOT REPORTED; Amortization: NOT QUANTIFIED; Novelty: leave-one-out 15/21 pass

extractions.source_title: TSCG: Deterministic Tool-Schema Compilation for Agentic LLM Deployments
extractions.fact: Schema compilation (JSON → structured text), not task binding. 8 deterministic operators, formal compression bound ≥51%
extractions.verbatim_quote: TSCG, a deterministic tool-schema compiler that resolves this mismatch by transforming JSON schemas into token-efficient structured text... TSCG combines eight composable operators with a formal compression bound (≥51% on well-formed schemas).
extractions.source_location: Abstract; Section 1; Section 3.1 (Eight Operators); Section 3.3 Theorem 3.1; Section 3.5
extractions.extracted_value: Token savings: 50-72%; Formal bound: ≥51%; BFCL ARR: 108-181%; Phi-4 14B: 0%→84.4% (20 tools), 90.3% (50 tools); Format-vs-compression R²=0.88→0.03
extractions.runnability_evidence: 1,200-line zero-dependency TypeScript package. Sub-millisecond execution. No model access, fine-tuning, or runtime search. GitHub: SKZL-AI/tscg
extractions.task_distribution_comparability: INCOMPARABLE: Schema compression benchmark (TAB ~19K calls, BFCL, GSM8K) vs SPIDER alias-OOD (parameterized HTTP routing). Different: schema compression vs task execution; function-calling/MCP schemas vs HTTP parameterized routing.
extractions.compilation_vs_inheritance_conflation: CLEAN - Pure deterministic compilation of schemas. 'TSCG is a *compiler*, not a search-based optimizer... same input always produces the same output. No model access is required' (Section 3.5).
extractions.staleness_maintenance_reported: NOT REPORTED. Section 7.4 discusses Community Schema Registry maintenance but no costs quantified.

extractions.source_title: TSCG: Deterministic Tool-Schema Compilation for Agentic LLM Deployments
extractions.fact: Sub-millisecond compilation; 50-72% token savings; ≥51% formal bound; not applicable regime (schema compilation, not task execution)
extractions.verbatim_quote: TSCG executes in <1 ms on commodity hardware; LLMLingua-2 requires 42.5 s on the same prompts (~40,000× slower)... Empirically we observe 61% (Scenario A), 66% (BFCL), and 75% (tool descriptions) savings.
extractions.extracted_value: Build cost: <1ms; Token savings: 50-72% (52-57% on heavy MCP); Formal bound: ≥51%; No reuse count/novelty/task length (schema regime)
extractions.runnability_evidence: Zero deps, no LLM, no browser, no Docker

extractions.source_title: Compiled AI: Deterministic Code Generation for LLM-Based Workflow Automation
extractions.fact: YAML spec → template selection → one-time LLM generation → 4-stage validation → deterministic Temporal activity; Code Factory variant for semantic tasks
extractions.verbatim_quote: A workflow system satisfying three properties: (1) one-time LLM invocation... (2) zero LLM invocations in the control plane... (3) mandatory multi-stage validation... Compiled AI achieves 96% task completion with zero runtime tokens, breaking even with runtime inference at approximately 17 transactions and reducing token consumption by 57× at 1,000 transactions.
extractions.source_location: Abstract; Section 1 Definition; Section 3 (System Architecture); Section 5 (Experiments); Section 6.1 Tables 1-2; Section 6.2 Table 3
extractions.extracted_value: BFCL: 96% completion, break-even n=17, 57x token reduction at 1K, 450x latency (4.5ms vs 2004ms), TCO $555 vs $22K (40x). DocILE Code Factory: KILE 80.0%, LIR 80.4%. Control-plane determinism: 100% reproducibility, H=0.
extractions.runnability_evidence: Requires LLM for compilation (Claude Opus 4.5); execution on Temporal. Not runnable without LLM key + Temporal infrastructure.
extractions.task_distribution_comparability: INCOMPARABLE: BFCL (function-calling, 400 instances) + DocILE (document intelligence, 5,680 invoices) vs SPIDER alias-OOD (parameterized HTTP routing). Different: function-calling/document-intelligence vs web navigation; requires Temporal vs no infrastructure.
extractions.compilation_vs_inheritance_conflation: MOSTLY CLEAN - One-time generation from spec → deterministic execution. Code Factory uses bounded LLM tool calls at runtime for semantic subtasks, but orchestration compiled. No behavioral recording from prior executions.
extractions.staleness_maintenance_reported: Bounded tool call drift: 'semantic drift in extracted values requires production monitoring... evaluation does not characterize this drift over long deployment horizons' (Limitations). Model updates may require re-validation.
